title: Constructible approximation for the eight assertions
statement: Let k be algebraically closed, f : C \to \operatorname{Spec} k a curve [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting], and \Lambda a finite commutative ring. If the eight assertions [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions] hold for every constructible \Lambda-module sheaf on C [def-constructible-constructible], they hold for every torsion \Lambda-module sheaf F [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf] on C.

source.place: Theorem 03SC proof, first two paragraphs; Proposition 03SI for reduction

proof.text: The curve is Noetherian, quasi-compact and quasi-separated by its finite-type structure morphism. Use lem-pbc-u2-constructible-subobject-presentation to obtain a filtered diagram of constructible module subobjects of F, with actual colimit vertex F. Apply H at each stage. Forgetting coefficients preserves the cocone by lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-sheaves-forget-colimits.

For any qcqs scheme, reindex an abelian filtered cocone of universe u+1 along the directed final functor of lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-exists-directed-final. Apply lem-weil-pbc-etale-directed-cohomology-colimit and transfer its colimit property to Sheaf.functorH by lem-weil-pbc-sheafH-ext-derived-comparison. Reflect back along the final functor. This is the proved private helper sheafH_colimit; it keeps each canonical leg.

For C1 and C2 every class comes from a stage by Mathlib Concrete.isColimit_exists_rep; that stage is subsingleton, so the class is zero. For C3, the stalk functor preserves monomorphisms. Injectivity of the stalk map transfers p-power annihilation from F to each stage, giving the same class argument. The two stalk inheritance lemmas are proved directly using finite-limit preservation and ModuleCat.mono_iff_injective. C4 and C5 assume F itself is constructible; obtain these fields directly from H(F), without any finite-colimit claim.

For C6 and C7, the base-changed scheme is qcqs by pullback stability of separation and quasi-compactness. Abelian inverse image is a left adjoint, hence preserves the supplied cocone. The closed source lemma Etale.cohomologyMap_map gives a natural transformation between the two cohomology functors. Both preserve this diagram's colimit by the private continuity helper. Stagewise bijectivity gives stagewise IsIso, then Mathlib isIso_app_coconePt_of_preservesColimit gives IsIso at F, hence bijectivity. For C6, stalk injectivity transfers invertible-order torsion to each constructible subobject; C7 needs no order restriction.

For C8 every open subscheme is Noetherian, hence qcqs. Inverse image and cohomology send the supplied diagram to a colimit on that open. Represent a target H2 class at one stage, lift it by the stage's C8, and map the lift into H2(C,F). Etale.cohomologyMap_map identifies its restriction with the represented target class. Assemble these eight fields in the unchanged Assertions structure. No arbitrary construction of elements, finiteness of a filtered colimit, or new cohomology axiom is used.

proof_origin.place: 03SC first proof paragraph; U2 Lean image presentation, directed continuity, stalk inheritance, and explicit eight-field assembly. Read sources at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03SC, /03SA and /09BH.

theorem IsCurve.assertions_of_constructible_approximation
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ] {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {C : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve f]
    (H : ∀ (G : Sheaf C.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
      [Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf G], IsCurve.Assertions Λ f G)
    (F : Sheaf C.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) [Scheme.IsTorsionSheaf F] :
    IsCurve.Assertions Λ f F
